claims.claim: On the tRPC benchmark, codeblast's predicted affected-test set contained every test file that actually failed, for all 28 mutants the test suite killed.
claims.metric: mutation-testing recall: fraction of killed mutants whose real failing-test file set is a subset of the predicted affected-test file set
claims.method: 30 mutants injected one at a time into test-covered TypeScript functions (throw on the function's first line); the full vitest suite is run per mutant to obtain the ground-truth failing-test files; the file is then restored. 2 of the 30 mutants were not killed by the suite (dead code path or type-only) and are excluded from the ratio.

claims.claim: Mean precision of the tRPC impact prediction over the same 28 killed mutants is 0.358, so most predicted affected tests did not fail.
claims.metric: arithmetic mean of per-mutant precision (predicted affected tests that really failed / predicted affected tests), both channels combined
claims.method: Same mutation run as trpc-mutation-impact-recall; the per-mutant precision field of the 28 killed mutants is averaged. Over-approximation is deliberate: the engine prefers false positives to false negatives.
claims.repro: python3 -c "import json,statistics;d=json.load(open('eval/mutation-2026-08-28-trpc-n30.json'));print(round(statistics.mean([e['precision'] for e in d if 'precision' in e]),3))"

claims.claim: On the graphql-tools benchmark (npm workspaces + jest), all 10 mutants were recalled with no missed affected test file.
claims.metric: mutation-testing recall on a second benchmark repository, using the jest runner
claims.method: Same harness with --runner jest against ardatan/graphql-tools. Suspected misses are re-run on restored source; a test that still fails without the mutation is judged flaky and removed from the ground truth. Mean precision over the 10 mutants is 0.331.

claims.claim: On a 15-mutant tRPC run the call-graph channel alone reaches mean precision 0.744, while the combined two-channel prediction recalls 15 of 15 mutants.
claims.metric: arithmetic mean of per-mutant precision_call (call-graph-reachable predictions only)
claims.method: 15-mutant run recording both channels per mutant: precision for the combined call+import prediction and precision_call for the call-graph-reachable subset. recall_hit is true for all 15 mutants.
claims.repro: python3 -c "import json,statistics;d=json.load(open('eval/mutation-2026-08-31-trpc-n15.json'));print(round(statistics.mean([e['precision_call'] for e in d]),3), sum(e['recall_hit'] for e in d), len(d))"

claims.claim: Dropping the conservative import channel and keeping only call-graph edges raises call-channel precision to 0.702 but collapses recall to 2 of 14 killed mutants.
claims.metric: recall of a call-graph-only impact prediction, and the mean precision it buys, on a controlled channel-ablation run
claims.method: Channel ablation on tRPC: for each mutant both the combined prediction and the call-only prediction are scored against the same ground truth. 1 of 15 mutants was not killed by the suite and is excluded, leaving 14; call_recall_hit is true for 2 of them and mean precision_call is 0.702.
claims.repro: python3 -c "import json,statistics;d=[e for e in json.load(open('eval/mutation-2026-08-28-trpc-n15-channel.json')) if 'precision' in e];print(sum(e['call_recall_hit'] for e in d), len(d), round(statistics.mean([e['precision_call'] for e in d]),3))"

claims.claim: Replayed over 50 consecutive real tRPC commits, the PR bot produced no comment on 42 of them and completed all 50 runs without error.
claims.metric: count of replayed commits for which pr-comment emitted empty stdout, over 50 non-merge commits
claims.method: eval/pr_replay.py walks 50 non-merge commits of trpc/trpc origin/main and runs pr-comment on each commit against its parent, recording ok, silent, seconds and comment_lines per commit.

claims.claim: Independent blind review rated the PR bot's comments 25%, 75%, 57% and 20% useful across four rounds, all below the project's own 87.5% self-rating of the first window.
claims.metric: share of emitted PR comments rated useful rather than noise or misleading, by a blind reviewer that did not build the tool
claims.method: Four rounds recorded in intent.md: 2/8 on the first replay window, 9/12 on a second 50-commit window, 4/7 on a third window (skip=100), 1/5 on a re-run of that window after fixes. The 87.5% figure is the author agent rating its own 8 comments; intent.md records the gap as evidence of reviewer bias. Reviewed comment bodies are committed under eval/pr-replay-2026-08-28-window2 (12 files) and eval/pr-replay-2026-08-28-window3 (7 files).
claims.repro: python3 eval/pr_replay.py 100 /tmp/pr-replay, then re-rate the comments against eval/pr-replay-2026-08-28-window3

claims.claim: The weekly acceptance workflow fails the build if the tRPC graph drops below 900 files or 15000 edges, or the graphql-tools graph below 300 files or 8000 edges.
claims.value: tRPC > 900 files and > 15000 edges; graphql-tools > 300 files and > 8000 edges
claims.metric: hard assertions on files and edges row counts in the generated SQLite graph, used as sentinels against silent file loss
claims.method: The acceptance workflow indexes each benchmark repo, asserts the row counts, then runs mutation testing behind a 100% recall gate; a scheduled failure opens an issue labelled acceptance-regression.

claims.claim: Indexing the tRPC monorepo produces a 6248-node, 17072-edge graph across 957 files with zero failures.
claims.value: 957 files, 6248 nodes, 17072 edges, 14725 blind spots, 0 failures
claims.metric: row counts reported by `codeblast index` for the generated SQLite graph; blind_spots counts unresolved and dynamic references, which is expected to be large on a real TypeScript monorepo and is not an error count
claims.method: Single `codeblast index` run of published codeblast 0.3.0 against a shallow clone of trpc/trpc at commit 66d0544. Deterministic given the same commit and version; counts drift with upstream commits, so the commit is part of the claim. Wall-clock seconds are machine-dependent and deliberately not claimed.
claims.repro: git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/trpc/trpc.git && git -C trpc checkout 66d0544 && npx codeblast@0.3.0 index ./trpc --db /tmp/graph.db
